stories.headline: Kyiv’s corruption scandal threatens Zelenskyy’s EU push New charges against a former aide test Ukraine’s claim that it is ready for fast-track membership.
stories.summary: Ukraine's former presidential aide, Andriy Yermak, has been named a suspect in a money-laundering scheme by the country's anti-corruption agencies. Yermak, who resigned in November, appeared in a Kyiv court and is being investigated as part of "Operation Midas." The scandal threatens to damage Ukraine's image abroad and hinder its push for fast-track EU membership. President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has called for Ukraine's admission to the EU by next year, but the bloc's leaders consider this target unrealistic due to ongoing corruption issues. Endemic corruption is a significant obstacle to Ukraine's EU accession, and this latest investigation has reached deep into Zelenskyy's former inner circle, embarrassing the Ukrainian leader as he seeks Western financing and EU membership. The investigation is a major challenge to Zelenskyy's government, which has faced its biggest threat since Russia's full-scale invasion.

stories.headline: EU to ban Brazilian meat imports from September The ban would come just two weeks after the EU-Mercosur trade deal provisionally entered into force, liberalising agricultural trade across the Atlantic despite
stories.summary: The EU will ban Brazilian meat imports starting September, just two weeks after the EU-Mercosur trade deal provisionally enters into force. The deal liberalizes agricultural trade across the Atlantic, despite opposition from farmers. Brazil has confirmed the EU's move to block its animal product exports. Meanwhile, the EU-Mercosur Interim Trade Agreement will be provisionally applied, allowing EU producers to benefit from the deal. The EU currently imports 82% of its niobium, a key component in MRI scanners and cancer treatment, from Mercosur countries. The trade agreement aims to formalize this supply relationship, supporting the EU's green and digital transition ambitions. The ban on Brazilian meat imports will take effect in September, amid the newly implemented trade agreement. The EU's decision to block Brazilian animal products is seen as a significant development in the trade relationship between the two regions.

stories.headline: Major ICE crackdown on 10,000 foreign students on OPT; 'fake companies' being operated from India US News: The Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) announced a major crackdown on an immigration program that allows international students to work tempora.
stories.summary: The US Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) has launched a crackdown on a program allowing international students to work temporarily in the US after graduating. Over 10,000 potential fraud cases have been identified, involving foreign students claiming work employment to prolong their stay. The students, mostly on Optional Practical Training (OPT), allegedly worked for "fake companies" operated from India. ICE's investigation aims to protect America from cross-border crime and illegal immigration. The crackdown comes as the number of new foreign undergraduate students at US colleges has dropped by 20% this spring, according to a recent study. ICE is part of the Department of Homeland Security, tasked with finding, detaining, and deporting undocumented immigrants. The agency's mission is to ensure national security and public safety. The crackdown targets fraudulent activities exploiting the OPT program.

stories.headline: Trump wants to rebrand ICE as NICE. Not everyone agrees President Donald Trump has made clear on social media and in interviews that he thinks Immigration and Customs Enforcement needs a rebrand — more specifically,
stories.summary: President Donald Trump wants to rebrand Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) as National Immigration and Customs Enforcement (NICE). Trump has expressed this idea on social media and in interviews, suggesting a name change is needed. ICE was established in 2002 as part of the Homeland Security Act, following the September 11 attacks, and absorbed functions from the Immigration and Naturalization Service and the US Customs Service. The proposed rebranding is seen as a public relations move, rather than a legal renaming. Trump has already endorsed the concept on his platform, with some conservative voices supporting the idea online. However, not everyone agrees with the proposed name change, sparking debate about the potential rebranding of ICE. The move is currently a concept, with no official changes announced.

stories.headline: Marvel Rivals Version 20260515 Balance Post Marvel Rivals is a Super Hero Team-based PVP Shooter in the Marvel Universe developed by Marvel Games & NetEase Games, has already launched globally with All He
stories.summary: Marvel Rivals, a free-to-play hero shooter video game, has launched globally with all heroes available to unlock. Developed by NetEase Games in collaboration with Marvel Games, the game is a Super Hero Team-based PVP Shooter set in the Marvel Universe. Players assemble a team of Marvel characters and engage in 6v6 battles, utilizing unique Team-Up skills and strategies. The game features destructible and ever-changing battlefields across the Marvel universe. Recent updates include a balance patch for Season 7 and a preview of Season 8. A guide for playing as Devil Dinosaur has also been released, outlining abilities and best team compositions. The game's developer vision has been shared, providing insight into the game's future updates and developments. Marvel Rivals is available to play, offering a dynamic and evolving gaming experience.

stories.headline: Sony's New Wearable Air Conditioner Keeps You Cooler Than Ever Forget portable fans. This new Reon Pocket Pro Plus runs 20% cooler than previous models, which Sony says will result in a 2-degree Celsius reduction in body te
stories.summary: Sony's Reon Pocket Pro Plus, a wearable air conditioner, has been upgraded to run 20% cooler than previous models. This improvement is expected to result in a 2-degree Celsius reduction in body temperature. The device features new fins that increase stability by 40%, holding it securely on the neck and shoulders. The Reon Pocket Pro Plus offers enhanced cooling performance, improved stability, and smarter temperature monitoring. Sony has made this latest model available in Europe and the UK, expanding its reach. The device's cooling performance and stability upgrades aim to provide a more effective and comfortable wearable cooling solution. With its improved features, the Reon Pocket Pro Plus is positioned as a unique and innovative gadget in Sony's lineup.

stories.headline: Yamaha Unveils Two New Affordable Home Theater AV Receivers The RX300A and RX500A add a new dimension to the brand’s entry- and step-up AV receiver lineup
stories.summary: Yamaha has introduced two new affordable home theater AV receivers, the RX300A and RX500A. The RX300A is a 5.2-channel Dolby Atmos AV receiver, succeeding the entry-tier Yamaha RX-V385, while the RX500A is a 7.2-channel Dolby Atmos AV receiver, introducing a new price and performance tier. Both models feature a modern design, Dolby Atmos immersion, 4K/120Hz HDMI for gamers, enhanced streaming, and simplified operation. The RX300A will be available in June 2026 for $399.95, and the RX500A will be available in September 2026 for $599.95. These new receivers aim to deliver immersive home-theater sound and the latest video and streaming capabilities to a wider range of entertainment lovers. They will be available from Yamaha and authorized dealers.

stories.headline: Donaldson Honors Patent Recipients and Inventor Award Winners Donaldson Company, Inc. (NYSE:DCI), a leading worldwide manufacturer of innovative filtration products and solutions, announced its calendar year 2025 Patent
stories.summary: Donaldson Company, Inc. honored its patent recipients and inventor award winners for calendar year 2025. The company, a leading manufacturer of filtration products and solutions, recognized employees in various categories, including Emerging Innovator, Manufacturing Excellence, and Technology Champion. Winners of these awards reside in Belgium and the United States. This recognition is part of Donaldson's efforts to advance filtration technology and promote innovation. The company has a long history of innovation, dating back over 11 decades, and continues to identify problems and develop solutions to address them. Donaldson's filtration products are used in various industries, including commercial, aerospace, chemical, and pharmaceuticals, and the company is committed to advancing its Filtration for a Thriving Future strategy. The awards ceremony is an annual event, with the previous year's ceremony honoring select employees for their groundbreaking contributions.

stories.headline: Florentino Perez refuses to be drawn on Jose Mourinho return to Real Madrid when calling presidential elections & inviting competition for control at Santiago Bernabeu
stories.summary: Real Madrid president Florentino Perez has announced plans to call presidential elections, inviting competition for control of the club. Perez stated he will run in the elections to defend the club's member-owned structure. When asked about speculation linking Jose Mourinho to a return as manager, Perez refused to comment, saying "we are not at that stage of the process." He emphasized his commitment to the club and its members, stating he will not leave unless the members want him to. Perez's announcement comes amid reports of potential coaching changes, but he declined to discuss the team's results or coaching situation, focusing instead on the upcoming elections and his desire to protect the club's ownership model. The elections are expected to take place this year, with Perez encouraging other candidates to run.

stories.headline: IPL 2026: GT storm to top of table as Kagiso Rabada leads SRH demolition in 82-run thrashing
stories.summary: Gujarat Titans outclassed Sunrisers Hyderabad by 82 runs in Ahmedabad, taking them to the top of the IPL 2026 points table. The team extended their winning streak to five matches with a commanding all-round display. Kagiso Rabada led the demolition, taking 3 wickets for 28 runs and breaking the top order. The Sunrisers Hyderabad innings collapsed under the pressure of the Gujarat Titans' pace attack. The result solidified Gujarat Titans' position at the top of the table, with the team continuing their brilliant winning streak. The 82-run thrashing marked a significant victory for Gujarat Titans, showcasing their strength in the IPL 2026 season. With this win, they have established themselves as a strong contender in the tournament.

stories.headline: Ruby Tui: ‘I’m going for France - the game needs someone to stop England’
stories.summary: New Zealand rugby union player Ruby Tui believes France can end England's 37-game winning streak in their upcoming match in Bordeaux. Tui, a popular TV presenter and former Olympic silver medalist, thinks France has the potential to stop England. The match is scheduled for Sunday, and Tui's comments come ahead of the highly anticipated game. England's Red Roses have been on a dominant run, but Tui thinks France can break their winning streak. As a seasoned player who has competed internationally, including at the 2016 Summer Olympics, Tui's opinion carries weight. She has been part of the New Zealand Women's Sevens team since 2012 and has experience in high-pressure games. Tui's comments add to the excitement and anticipation surrounding the upcoming match between France and England.

stories.headline: Lakers’ GM Rob Pelinka Wants to Honor LeBron James With Space to Make Retirement Decision
stories.summary: Los Angeles Lakers General Manager Rob Pelinka has stated that the team wants to give LeBron James space to make a decision about his potential retirement. Following the team's postseason elimination, Pelinka spoke to the press, leaving the door open for James to return next season if he chooses to do so. The 41-year-old James has not set a retirement timeline and has expressed uncertainty about when he will walk away from the game. Pelinka and Coach JJ Redick have affirmed their desire to keep James with the Lakers if he decides to continue playing. The team intends to honor James by giving him time to determine his own intentions for a possible 24th NBA season. Pelinka emphasized that the decision is entirely up to James, with the team waiting for his decision.

stories.headline: ‘Don’t want to be part of biased exercise’: Rahul Gandhi records dissent on CBI director’s selection
stories.summary: Rahul Gandhi has recorded a dissent note during the CBI director selection meeting, citing a lack of transparency and denial of crucial candidate information by the government. He alleged that the government has misused the CBI to target political opponents, journalists, and critics. Gandhi stated that the Leader of Opposition is included in the Selection Committee to prevent institutional capture, but he was denied a meaningful role in the process. He referred to his earlier dissent recorded on May 5 last year and a letter to the Prime Minister on October 21, suggesting measures for a fair and transparent selection process. Gandhi expressed that he does not want to be part of a biased exercise, highlighting the need for transparency in the CBI director's selection. The dissent note was submitted during the selection meeting, marking a strong objection to the process.

stories.headline: India criticises China, raises 'reputation' question over support to Pakistan
stories.summary: India has criticized China for its support to Pakistan, questioning China's reputation. The criticism comes after Chinese claims of providing "on-site support" to Pakistan during a conflict, which India's Ministry of External Affairs says corroborates earlier knowledge. China's involvement with Pakistan has been significant, with Pakistan being the only known operator of certain Chinese aircraft outside of China. Chinese employees have spoken about providing support to Pakistan, highlighting the jet's performance during hostilities. China's military support for Pakistan has increased in recent years, with Pakistani PM Shehbaz Sharif praising China as a "most reliable friend" amid regional tensions. China has reaffirmed its support for Pakistan's sovereignty and called for a fair probe into a recent attack, further straining relations with India.

stories.headline: Rahul Gandhi dissents on CBI chief selection: 'Leader of Opposition is not a rubber stamp'
stories.summary: Rahul Gandhi expressed dissent over the CBI Director selection process, stating that the Leader of Opposition is not a rubber stamp. He wrote to Prime Minister Narendra Modi, claiming he did not receive a response to his suggestions. Gandhi said he cannot participate in the biased exercise and is dissenting in the strongest terms. He emphasized that the Leader of the Opposition's role in the Selection Committee is to prevent institutional capture, but he has been denied a meaningful role. This is not the first time Gandhi has recorded his dissent, having done so previously on May 5, 2025. A new CBI chief is expected to be selected soon, with Gandhi's dissent noting his opposition to the current selection process. He reiterated that he will not abdicate his constitutional duty by participating in the process.

stories.headline: AIADMK rebel MLAs to back TVK in Tamil Nadu floor test
stories.summary: Rebel AIADMK MLAs, led by S P Velumani and C Ve Shanmugam, have pledged support to TVK in the Tamil Nadu Assembly floor test, opposing the confidence motion by Palaniswami's faction. The rebel faction, comprising around 30 MLAs, met with Chief Minister Vijay and submitted a letter backing his government bid. This development signals a major escalation in the power struggle within Tamil Nadu's principal opposition party. The rebel leaders announced their decision to split from Palaniswami's leadership, citing their reasons. With the support of the rebel MLAs, TVK is likely to gain an advantage in the floor test, scheduled to take place on Wednesday. The move is seen as a significant shift in the state's political landscape, with the rebel faction's backing potentially influencing the outcome of the floor test.

stories.headline: [Bloomberg] S&P 500, Nasdaq Futures Drop With Inflation in Focus, Oil Surges on Geopolitics
stories.summary: US stock indices opened lower, with the S&P 500 down 0.42% and Nasdaq futures off 0.54%, as higher-than-expected April inflation data sparked concerns. Oil prices surged due to worsening tensions between the US and Iran, further impacting market sentiment. The Nasdaq dropped 0.7% and S&P 500 slipped at the open, as traders pulled back from risk assets. The inflation data came in hotter than economists' estimates, while rising tensions in the Middle East drove crude prices higher. Investors are awaiting further developments, with the tech rally's sustainability also a concern. The surge in oil prices and inflation concerns have led to a decline in US equities, which had previously seen a strong run. The market is closely watching the situation, with the US-Iran tensions and inflation data being key factors influencing investor decisions.

stories.headline: [Firstpost] Critical minerals, Taiwan and AI wars: Trump-Xi meeting could reshape global geopolitics
stories.summary: The upcoming Trump-Xi summit in Beijing is expected to have significant implications for global geopolitics. The meeting, the first since Trump's re-election, comes amid growing tensions between the US and China. Key issues on the agenda include critical minerals, such as rare earth elements, which are essential for defense equipment and modern technology. The US is also concerned about China's influence over Taiwan and the ongoing rivalry in artificial intelligence. The summit follows a previous meeting in October, where the leaders agreed to reduce tariffs and address the flow of illicit drugs into the US. The outcome of the meeting could potentially lead to a 'G2' formation, with the US and China forming a bilateral partnership to address global issues. The talks will also be influenced by the Iran crisis and other regional tensions.

stories.headline: [MarketScreener] Torex Gold is Riding a Wave but for How Long?
stories.summary: Torex Gold Resources Inc. reported a significant increase in net income for the first quarter ended March 31, 2026, with $207.5 million compared to $39 million a year ago. The company benefited from selling 81,233 oz of gold at new prices, resulting in an additional $162 million in revenue compared to last year's prices. This surge in earnings has raised questions about the company's ability to sustain quarterly earnings of $200 million. The recent performance has been impressive, but the real test lies in maintaining this level of profitability in the future. Torex Gold's stock has been closely watched, with investors and analysts monitoring the company's progress and providing recommendations for stock trading and investing. The company's financials and technical analysis are available on MarketScreener.

stories.summary: A Texas couple is suing an AI company, alleging it guided their teenage son to use drugs, resulting in a fatal overdose. Meanwhile, NYU Langone Health received a federal grand jury subpoena regarding gender-affirming care provided to minors. Inflation has surged to 3.8% in April, exceeding wage growth for the first time since 2023. Louisiana officials have agreed to a $4.8 million settlement with the family of Ronald Greene, a Black motorist who died during a violent 2019 arrest. Additionally, the World Health Organization is working to contain hantavirus after evacuations, with the head stating "our work is not over." These developments come as global leaders, including US President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping, continue to meet and discuss international issues, as seen in their recent bilateral meeting in South Korea.

stories.headline: Stock Markets Plunge as West Asia Tensions, High Oil Price Fuel Sell-Off Indian equity benchmark indices, Sensex and Nifty, tumbled nearly 2 per cent for the fourth consecutive session, driven by elevated crude oil prices, escalating
stories.summary: Indian equity benchmark indices, Sensex and Nifty, fell nearly 2% for the fourth consecutive session due to elevated crude oil prices and escalating US-Iran tensions. Brent crude traded 2.75% higher at $107.1 per barrel, fueling market concerns. The Sensex plunged 1,456.04 points, or 1.92%, while the rupee depreciated 35 paise to an all-time low of 95.63 against the US dollar. The decline reflects caution around crude oil prices, West Asia tensions, and the broader earnings season. Surging crude oil prices triggered widespread selling pressure across sectors, with banking shares also hit by SBI's weaker-than-expected Q4 results. The market sentiment remains clouded by uncertainty surrounding the West Asia conflict and high oil prices.

stories.headline: Sensex Slumps 2,185 Points In 5 Days To 75,124, Investors Lose ₹11 Lakh Crore As Market Weakness Deepens Indian stock markets extended losses for the fourth straight session as Sensex slipped to 75,124 and Nifty fell to 23,565. Rising crude oil prices, weak rupee,
stories.summary: Indian stock markets extended losses for the fourth straight session, with the Sensex slipping to 75,124 and Nifty falling to 23,565. The Sensex crashed over 1,400 points, with a drop of as much as 1,370.79 points during intraday trade. Rising crude oil prices, a weak rupee, and AI fears hammering IT stocks contributed to the market weakness. The losses resulted in investors losing nearly ₹11 lakh crore. Geopolitical tensions and persistent foreign fund outflows also played a role in the market downturn. Over five days, the Sensex slumped 2,185 points, deepening market weakness. The rupee hit a record low, and crude oil prices topped $107, further exacerbating the situation. The combined effects led to a significant decline in the Indian stock markets.

stories.headline: War Shock, Weak Growth: Why Sensex and Nifty Could Stay Flat for Years What is driving down the Indian stock market? Is this down phase ‘temporary’ and would it see reversal sometime soon? Or are Sensex and Nifty in for a long-term
stories.summary: The Indian stock market has experienced a sharp downturn, with the Sensex falling 3,000 points over nine sessions. The Nifty and Sensex have been driven down by aggressive Foreign Portfolio Investor (FPI) selling, global trade tensions, and weak earnings. In just five days, the market saw a 2,300-point drop. The smallcap and microcap segments have been particularly affected. Global events, including war and weak growth, are contributing to the market's volatility. The GIFT Nifty has also fallen, down 167 points. Key levels to watch will be crucial in determining the market's direction today. The combination of internal and external factors has led to a significant decline in the Indian stock market, with no clear indication of a reversal in the near term.

stories.headline: Stock market today (May 12, 2026): Which are top 10 gainers and losers on NSE & BSE? Check list India Business News: Indian equity benchmark indices extended losses for the fourth straight session on Tuesday, with the Sensex and Nifty plunging nearly 2 per
stories.summary: Indian equity benchmark indices extended losses for the fourth straight session on Tuesday, with the Sensex and Nifty plunging nearly 2 per cent. The Sensex fell 1,312 points, while the Nifty dropped 360 points, amid rising oil prices. The BSE Sensex currently stands at 77,328.19, down 516.33 points, or 0.66 per cent. The NSE also experienced a decline. The top gainers and losers on the NSE and BSE have been reported, with various corporate announcements made, including a board meeting intimation by Shriram Asset Management Company Ltd. The downturn is attributed to renewed military tensions and profit-booking across sectors, leading to a decline in investor sentiment. The Bank Nifty, comprising 12 major bank stocks, also experienced a decline, reflecting the overall market trend.

stories.headline: 'Shock Is Coming': Uday Kotak Backs PM, Issues Warning Over Iran War
stories.summary: Uday Kotak, a prominent industry leader, has warned that India should prepare for the worst due to the potential impact of a US-Iran war on global energy prices. He stated that the effects of the Middle East conflict have not yet been fully transmitted to consumers and businesses in India, but "it's coming." Kotak backed Prime Minister Modi's call for restrained spending, emphasizing the importance of financial discipline to mitigate the impact of oil shocks and global instability on India's economy. With crude oil prices rising sharply due to uncertainty around the US-Iran ceasefire, Kotak cautioned that India needs to be prepared for the impending "shock" and stressed the need for stronger financial discipline to navigate the challenging times ahead. His remarks were made at the CII Annual Business Summit 2026 in Delhi.

stories.headline: Microsoft May 2026 Patch Tuesday fixes 120 flaws, no zero-days
stories.summary: Microsoft's May 2026 Patch Tuesday addresses 120 vulnerabilities, with no zero-days disclosed this month, the first such month since June 2024. The updates include fixes for three critical Remote Code Execution (RCE) flaws with CVSS scores of 9.8 or higher, affecting Netlogon, Windows DNS Client, and Microsoft Dynamics 365. A total of 13 critical flaws were patched, along with other vulnerabilities. Key areas of concern include Azure, Windows DNS, and Dynamics 365. The patches are part of Microsoft's regular monthly security updates, aiming to protect users from potential exploits. This month's patch count is slightly lower than the 137 vulnerabilities fixed in the previous month.

stories.headline: PowerSchool hack was a ‘significant breach,’ says N.L. privacy commissioner
stories.summary: A significant data breach occurred at PowerSchool, a school software firm, affecting hundreds of thousands of people in Newfoundland, including children. The breach, deemed a "significant breach" by Information and Privacy Commissioner Kerry Hatfield, exposed personal information, including MCP numbers of 244 individuals, and teacher data dating back to 2010. An internal report revealed that the breach was caused by a basic security oversight, with an executive admitting that a breached account had not used multi-factor authentication. The incident has sparked calls for stricter laws to regulate companies and protect personal information, with the privacy commissioner stating that laws need to be put in place to keep companies in check. The breach is expected to have significant implications for the ed-tech industry.

stories.headline: Swatch gains after surviving activist investor's bid to shake up the board
stories.summary: Swatch shareholders have rejected a bid by activist investor Greenwood to gain a seat on the company's board, allowing the Hayek family to retain control. The decision has led to a gain in Swatch's stock price. This move is part of a larger trend of activist investors attempting to shake up companies' boards and strategies. Similar attempts have been made at other companies, such as Barclays, where an activist investor has built up a 5% stake to influence the bank's strategy. Additionally, Elliott, another activist investor, has taken a $1B stake in BioMarin and guided Catalent in adding new independent directors to its board. These efforts aim to boost share prices and improve company performance. The Hayek family's control of Swatch remains unchanged following the rejected bid.
